title: Life as the Standard
summary: Life as the root of value, and one's own life as the standard of moral value.

lessons.title: Why Value Needs Life
lessons.objective: Recognize that the idea of value depends on a living being that can gain or lose its existence.

exercises.prompt: On this account, what makes the idea of value possible?

choices.text: A living being that can keep existing or cease to exist
A majority that agrees on a preference
A feeling that arrives with no reason
An inanimate object that never faces an alternative

feedback.note: Value is rooted in life. Only a living thing has something it can gain or lose by what it does.

exercises.prompt: Why does a rock not have values?

choices.text: Nothing it does can sustain or end a life of its own
Its values are real but hidden from observers
A law forbids rocks from valuing
Only large objects can have values

feedback.note: Without the alternative of life or non-life, there is nothing for or against which an action could count.

exercises.prompt: Match each thing to what this unit says about value.

pairs.right: Can face gain or loss of its existence
Has no stake that could make something a value
The root that makes value possible

feedback.note: Life is the root of value because only the living confront an alternative that matters.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about the root of value.

parts.text: , because only a living being can

feedback.note: Call life the root. The living being is the one for whom outcomes can be gains or losses.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names the root of value.

feedback.note: Life is the root of value, not a custom added after the fact and not a decoration.

exercises.prompt: If nothing were alive, what would follow for the idea of value?

choices.text: There would be no valuer and no values
Values would stay the same, only unnamed
Rocks would take over the role of valuers
Values would multiply without anyone to hold them

feedback.note: Value requires a living valuer. Remove life and the concept has nothing left to apply to.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to its role in this lesson.

feedback.note: Keep the three links: life is the root, the living are the valuers, and existence is what is at stake.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

parts.text: . An inanimate thing cannot, because it faces no alternative of

feedback.note: Valuing belongs to the living. The alternative that makes it possible is life or death.

exercises.prompt: Which statement fits this lesson?

choices.text: Life is the root of value
Value exists first, and life is added later as a hobby
Rocks and organisms are valuers in the same way
Nothing in reality is at stake for a living being

feedback.note: Start from life. Value is not a free-floating extra that living beings happen to notice.

lessons.title: The Alternative That Makes Good and Evil
lessons.objective: Explain that good and evil arise only where the alternative is life or death.

exercises.prompt: What alternative gives the words good and evil a meaning?

choices.text: Life or death for a living being
One flavor versus another flavor
One sports team versus another
One clothing style versus another

feedback.note: Good and evil name what furthers or works against life. Without that alternative, the words have no moral job.

exercises.prompt: Where nothing faces life or death, what happens to moral good and evil?

choices.text: They do not apply
They become stricter
They trade places every day
They attach to rocks instead

feedback.note: Moral good and evil presuppose a living being for whom existence is the alternative.

exercises.prompt: Match each side of the alternative to the evaluation it supports.

feedback.note: The alternative sets the direction: for life is good, against life is evil, and with no alternative the terms drop out.

exercises.prompt: Complete the alternative.

parts.text: The alternative that makes value possible is

feedback.note: Name the alternative as life or death. Taste and applause are not that alternative.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about where good and evil apply.

feedback.note: Good and evil presuppose life or death. They are not labels for a coin toss or a dress code.

exercises.prompt: A plant turns toward light and takes in water. In this unit, what does that illustrate?

choices.text: Even nonhuman life acts in ways that sustain it
A plant chooses a moral code
A plant has no relationship to the alternative of life or death
A plant waits for a vote before growing

feedback.note: Life is already the root of value for living organisms. A plant does not hold a moral code, but its life is still what its actions serve.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the right conclusion.

pairs.left: A stone sitting on a path
pairs.right: No values, because no life is at stake for it

pairs.left: A person who can live or die
pairs.right: A being for whom good and evil can apply

feedback.note: Organisms have a stake. A stone does not. A person is the kind of living being for whom moral judgment applies.

exercises.prompt: Fill the evaluations.

parts.text: . What works against life is the

feedback.note: The direction is fixed by life: for it is good, against it is evil.

exercises.prompt: Which pair is the alternative this lesson is about?

choices.text: Life or death
Hot or cold weather as such
Left hand or right hand
Old custom or new custom

feedback.note: Only life or death is the alternative that gives value, good, and evil their root.

lessons.title: Not a Whim or a Command
lessons.objective: Reject whim, crowd opinion, and a supernatural command as the root of value.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit refuse as the root of value?

choices.text: A whim, a crowd's opinion, or a supernatural command
The fact that a being is alive
The alternative of life or death
The requirements of one's own life

feedback.note: Life is the root. A passing wish, a poll, or an order from outside reality does not replace that root.

exercises.prompt: Someone says a thing is good only because they feel like it. What is wrong with that, on this account?

choices.text: A feeling does not replace life as the root of value
Feelings are always false reports of the facts
Feelings are forbidden in every context
Only a crowd is allowed to feel

feedback.note: A whim is not the standard. Whether something is a value depends on its relation to life, not on the wish of the moment.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed root to the verdict in this unit.

pairs.left: A command with no tie to life

feedback.note: Only life is the root. Whim, crowd preference, and a detached command are refused.

exercises.prompt: Complete the refusal.

parts.text: Value is not created by a

feedback.note: A whim does not create value. Life remains the root.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that rejects the crowd as the root.

feedback.note: Numbers do not turn a preference into the root of value. Life does that work.

exercises.prompt: A rule is announced as good solely because a supernatural authority said so, with no tie to life. How should this unit classify that rule?

choices.text: The command is not the root of value
The command replaces life as the root
Every command is automatically for one's life
The command gives values to inanimate matter

feedback.note: A command does not become the root of value by being announced. The root remains life.

exercises.prompt: Which question follows the root of value?

choices.text: Does this sustain a life, or work against it?
Did enough people clap?
Do I feel like it right now?
Was it ordered, regardless of life?

feedback.note: Once life is the root, the question is whether something sustains life or works against it.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states the root.

feedback.note: Life, not a command, is the root of value.

exercises.prompt: Match the test to what it actually checks.

pairs.right: A whim, not the root of value
A crowd's opinion, not the root of value
A relation to the root of value

feedback.note: Feeling and popularity do not establish value. A relation to life does.

lessons.title: One's Own Life as the Standard
lessons.objective: Identify one's own life as the standard used to judge moral good and evil for oneself.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is the standard of moral value?

choices.text: One's own life
No life in particular
Someone else's life in place of one's own
The absence of any standard

feedback.note: Life is the root of value, and the moral standard for a person is that person's own life.

exercises.prompt: What job does the standard do?

choices.text: It is what you judge moral good and evil by
It decorates a choice after the choice is made
It hides the fact that you are alive
It erases the difference between life and death

feedback.note: A standard of moral value is the measure for calling something good or evil. Here that measure is one's own life.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to the wording of this unit.

pairs.right: A stranger's life substituted for one's own

feedback.note: Keep root and standard distinct in wording: life is the root, and one's own life is the moral standard.

exercises.prompt: Complete the standard.

parts.text: The standard of moral value is one's own

feedback.note: One's own life is the standard. A whim is not.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names the moral standard.

feedback.note: One's own life is the standard of moral value.

exercises.prompt: Why is the standard one's own life rather than life with no owner?

choices.text: Moral judgment is about the life of the person who must choose
Morality is an average taken over nobody in particular
Each person is required to adopt a stranger as the standard
The chooser drops out of morality

feedback.note: The person who acts has a life to sustain. That life, not a life with no owner, is the moral standard.

exercises.prompt: Which substitution does this unit reject?

choices.text: Putting someone else's life in place of one's own as the standard
Using one's own life as the standard
Treating life as the root of value
Remembering the alternative of life or death

feedback.note: The standard is one's own life. Replacing it with another person's life changes the standard.

exercises.prompt: Fill both roles named in the unit summary.

parts.text: of value. One's own life is the

feedback.note: Use root for life as such, and standard for one's own life in moral judgment.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the answer this unit gives.

pairs.left: What is the root of value?
What is the standard of moral value?

pairs.right: The life of the person who must choose

feedback.note: Three answers stay fixed: life, one's own life, and the chooser's life as that standard.

exercises.prompt: A person asks how to judge an action morally. Which measure fits this unit?

choices.text: Whether it sustains or damages one's own life
Whether onlookers clap
Whether it matches a whim of the moment
Whether no standard is used at all

feedback.note: Moral judgment uses one's own life as the standard: sustain it or damage it.

lessons.title: For or Against That Life
lessons.objective: Judge an action as morally good when it sustains one's own life and as morally evil when it works against that life.

exercises.prompt: By the standard of one's own life, when is an action morally good?

choices.text: When it sustains one's own life
When it works against one's own life
When it is chosen at random
When a crowd would do the same thing for no reason tied to life

feedback.note: Good, under this standard, is what sustains one's own life. Working against that life is the opposite evaluation.

exercises.prompt: By the same standard, when is an action morally evil?

choices.text: When it works against one's own life
When it sustains one's own life
Whenever it is unpopular, even if it sustains one's life
Whenever it is unfamiliar

feedback.note: Evil is what works against one's own life. Unpopularity or unfamiliarity is not the standard.

exercises.prompt: Match each action, described only by its relation to one's life, to the moral evaluation.

pairs.left: Keeping the means of sustaining one's life
Choosing with no reference to one's life

feedback.note: Apply the standard directly: for one's life, against one's life, or not using the standard at all.

exercises.prompt: Complete the two evaluations.

parts.text: What sustains one's own life is morally
. What works against it is morally

feedback.note: The standard yields two directions: good when it sustains one's own life, evil when it works against that life.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule of evaluation.

feedback.note: The moral question is whether the action sustains one's own life.

exercises.prompt: An action feels exciting and also wrecks what one's life requires. How does the standard judge it?

choices.text: Morally evil, because it works against one's own life
Morally good, because the feeling was strong
Beyond judgment, because a feeling was present
A value for an inanimate object

feedback.note: The standard is one's own life, not the thrill. Working against that life is morally evil on this account.

exercises.prompt: An action is quiet and unfashionable, and it sustains one's own life. How does the standard judge it?

choices.text: Morally good, because it sustains one's own life
Morally evil, because it is unfashionable
Neither, because fashion was not involved in a loud way
Good only if a crowd copies it

feedback.note: Fashion is not the standard. Sustaining one's own life is what makes the action morally good here.

exercises.prompt: Name the standard inside the judgment.

parts.text: The measure is not a whim. The measure is one's own

feedback.note: One's own life is the measure. The good sustains it.

exercises.prompt: Match each mistake to what the standard actually says.

pairs.left: A strong feeling decides the good
pairs.right: No: one's own life is the standard

pairs.left: Harm to one's life can still be the good
pairs.right: No: that action is morally evil by this standard

pairs.left: Sustaining one's life is the good
pairs.right: Yes: that is the evaluation the standard gives

feedback.note: Feeling does not replace the standard. Harm to one's life is not the good. Sustaining that life is.
